content.text: Coverage confirmed: "solicitation" appears nowhere, and every "employee" reference is access-control (§ 8(c)) or indemnity boilerplate (§ 12). No non-solicit exists, so the compliant status holds. I'll resubmit with the rationale expanded to address the two failed parameter checks directly.

input.quote: b. Notification. Client shall not represent that loan underwriting decisions related to loans originated by using the Interface are in any way made by TrueLink
input.rationale:
Compliant because the agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant binding Mortgage Logic.com (Client), which is exactly our preferred position ("no non-solicit on Customer").

Scope of review: Section 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) is the natural home for a customer-side covenant and is limited to compliance with laws (8(a)), notification (8(b)), limitation on access (8(c)), Credit Data licensing (8(d)), content representations (8(e)), and spamming (8(f)). Section 10 (Confidentiality) imposes only information-protection duties with no personnel restriction. Full-text searches for "solicit", "solicitation", "employ", "employee", "induce", "hire", "recruit", "personnel", "staff", and "engage" surfaced only unsolicited-email/spam (§ 7), access control (§ 8(c)), indemnity boilerplate (§ 12), and a trademark-search obligation (§ 2) — none of which restrict either party's hiring. The sole "Non-Competition Agreement" cross-reference (§ 8(d)) limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data, not Client hiring.

On the two failed deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out): both are inapplicable rather than defective. Those parameters constrain the content of a non-solicit only if one exists; where no such covenant is imposed on the Customer, the absence of a duration cap and of a general-advertising carve-out cannot prejudice us, and is affirmative evidence of compliance with the preferred position. Accordingly no redline is proposed and no counterparty comment is warranted.

Fallback if TrueLink later proposes a non-solicit: mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and no "no-hire". Note for the deal team: the referenced Non-Competition Agreement is separate paper outside this document and should be reviewed against this rule in case it contains personnel restrictions binding us.
